title: Pipeline Validation - Paper Bridge
hook: Same paper. Why does changing the shape help?
payoff: The folded bridge resists bending more, without adding paper.
expectation: The same paper should respond the same way.
explanation: Folding changes the sheet's geometry and can make it more resistant to bending.

sources.title: Paper Bridge Challenge | Science of Strong Shapes

claims.text: Folding a sheet changes its shape and makes it more resistant to bending in this paper-bridge demonstration.
claims.conditions: A qualitative comparison of otherwise similar paper bridges and loading; no exact capacity or universal strength multiplier.

evidence.quote: When the paper is folded, its shape changes and it becomes more resistant to bending.

claims.reason: The institutional activity explicitly states this scoped change in bending resistance.

claims.text: The activity uses accordion-shaped folds running along the length of the bridge.
claims.conditions: The ANU paper bridge setup, using the same paper, supports and weights.

evidence.quote: Make sure the folds run along the length of the bridge.

claims.reason: The construction condition is explicit in the activity instructions.

review.notes: Existing project topic reused only as a technical validation sample. ANU page fetched successfully; Science Buddies returned HTTP 403 and is excluded. Qualitative animation, no measured capacity claims.

scenes.narration: Two bridges. Same kind of paper, same gap, same load. One stays much straighter. The difference is a few folds.
scenes.goal: Find why one sheet bends less.
scenes.action: Compare flat and folded bridges under a matching illustrated load.
scenes.nextBecause: Look at what changed between the sheets.

visual.heading: Same paper. Different result.
visual.prompt: Qualitative matched bridge comparison, no numerical capacity.

scenes.narration: A flat sheet bends easily. Fold the second sheet into an accordion, with the ridges running between the supports.
scenes.action: Show a folded bridge and the ridge direction.
scenes.nextBecause: Compare the cross-sections of the same sheet.

visual.heading: The folds run between the supports.
visual.prompt: Show longitudinal folds across the support gap.

scenes.narration: Those folds change the sheet's shape, making it more resistant to bending. We changed the geometry while keeping the same paper.
scenes.goal: Explain why the changed shape matters.
scenes.action: Show a close schematic view of flat and accordion cross-sections.
scenes.result: The geometric difference is easy to inspect.
scenes.nextBecause: Return to the original comparison to see its consequence.

scenes.narration: Add the same load again and compare. The folded bridge bends less in this demonstration. Same paper. A different shape, and a different result.
scenes.action: Return to both bridges and replay the matched qualitative load.

visual.heading: The shape makes the difference.
visual.prompt: Replay the qualitative comparison without any capacity numbers.
